name: Field_UpdateCullingFlag
summary: Per-actor distance culling: runs the base node culling update, then (when the field UI mode byte and the actor flags allow it) compares the squared distance to the position of the scene node at work+0x48 with the actor threshold at +0x25C and sets/clears bit 1 of the culling word at +0x50.
evidence: New context: the two mystery callees now have names - Gfx_Node_UpdateCullingFlag (the shared node-level culling step this function overrides for field actors) and Field_SceneNode_GetPosition (the position source). The old "player" wording is wrong; the source is the scene node at work+0x48, so the summary was corrected while the name was kept.

name: maybe_Ui_BuildListEntries
summary: Walks a 0xC-byte-stride record table obtained with func_0063F0B8(work, tableId), and for each row builds a 0x84-byte text/icon record: copies the 7-character name (std_wcsncpy), takes the icon byte through func_00149814/func_00158F94, measures the glyph run (func_0015141C) and centres it horizontally. The tail of the decompiled body is lost (it ends in std_Str_Length16 with three arguments), so what consumes the row is not visible.
evidence: Re-checked against the named callees: std_Str_Length16 is a real UTF-16 strlen (its own header proves it from the assembly), so the old "submits the row to 0x006121B4" claim in the summary was wrong - the function only measures the row, and the call is a damaged tail. No caller anywhere in decomp/readable, so the entry point is reached from a table and the name stays a maybe_.

name: Party_BuildStatusPanelData
summary: Builds the 0x40-byte text block of one party-status row: appends the character name and the level/HP/MP runs to the text buffer at work+0x50+200, then copies the finished 16-word block to *out (the caller stores it into its layout struct).
evidence: New caller context: maybe_Ui_MemberTable_Init (0x004AC46C) calls this once per row and copies the 16 words at local_f8 into its own layout block, which confirms that "out" is panel row data rather than a scratch buffer. Callees Game_GetDataManager/Game_GetWork/std_wcsncpy were already named.

name: maybe_Data_SetIndexedLabel
signature: void maybe_Data_SetIndexedLabel(int unusedCtx, int index, const u16* label)
summary: Clears four words of the 0x8C-byte-stride record at work+0x2AA7C+index*0x8C and copies the 7-character UTF-16 label into it (zero padding included).
evidence: The two callers (0x00309390, 0x002A73C8) pass a window field index and a window string pointer, not an actor id: they call maybe_Data_SetIndexedLabel(self, iVar1->f_51c, self+0x3558) and then measure that same string. The "actor" wording of the old name was unsupported (no actor code touches work+0x2AA7C); the offset is simply an 0x8C-stride label table, so the name was corrected to a structural one. Nothing proves what the table is for, hence still maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_CreateGridSystem
summary: Constructor of a 0x9C58-byte object: installs vtable 0x00782234, lazily creates a shared 0x10-stride pool, allocates the object plus a 400-entry array of 0x40-byte cells and constructs the collision/height sub-objects.
evidence: The callee names (Mem_AllocAligned_2, std_ConstructArray) confirm the allocation/array shape, but the only caller is Ui_TitleScreen_Ctor, which does not look like field grid setup, and 0x00782234 is the same vtable the actor status block uses. Grid semantics remain unproven, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Field2D_Scene_BuildFromFieldWork
summary: Adapter called by Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene6 at scene state 11: resolves the active 2D scene context (work+0x88 -> +8) and calls Field2D_Scene_BuildFromMapData with the scene object at fieldWork+0xC and the three bytes at +9/+0xA/+0xB.
evidence: Both sides are now named: the caller Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene6 passes its field work (self->f_8C) and the callee is Field2D_Scene_BuildFromMapData. The old "Gfx_Effect_ApplySetA" name was invented from an unnamed 0x005C1D64 and is wrong; this is the field-side wrapper that starts building the 2D scene.

name: Field2D_Scene_UpdateFromFieldWork
summary: Second half of the same adapter pair: called by Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene6 at scene state 12 and forwards the same field-work fields to Field2D_Scene_UpdateLayers, which refreshes the 2D scene layers.
evidence: The tail callee is now named Field2D_Scene_UpdateLayers and the caller is Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene6 (state 0xC branch, right after the build call). "Gfx_Effect_ApplySetB" described an effect set that does not exist in the body.

name: Ui_Window_CloseCurrentPane
summary: Closes the window's current pane: updates the pane widget at +0x1084, and if the object reference is the only variant it pops one pane and calls the pane virtual, otherwise it pops panes up to the default id and releases the object reference at +0x10D0.
evidence: All three callees are now named (Ui_Window_PopPane, Ui_Window_PopPaneUntilId, Container_ReleaseObjectRef), which pins the behaviour to closing the current pane. The old "ById" suffix was not supported by any argument - the function takes no id; the id is the global default the pop helper receives.

name: Ui_Window_PopPaneAndReleaseRef
summary: Pops the window's panes up to the default pane id and releases the object reference at +0x10D0. It is exactly the non-first-variant branch of Ui_Window_CloseCurrentPane.
evidence: The body is two named calls (Ui_Window_PopPaneUntilId + Container_ReleaseObjectRef) with no animation code at all, so "StartAnim" was wrong. It is the same helper pair as the branch in 0x00199250, hence the structural close-pane name.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetBottomScreenRect
summary: Configures a full 2D view on the graphics context: binds the range at +0x1308 to root+0x88 (mode 3) and writes the rectangle 0,0..240,400 into +0x1318..+0x1324. The three callers (EncountEventEx, Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle, maybe_Battle_CreateEnemyDisplay) are all full-screen 2D transition setups.
evidence: Callers are now named and confirm the "full-screen 2D pass before a battle transition" use, but 240x400 is the portrait orientation of the 400x240 LCD, so whether the code means the top or the bottom screen is not established. Name kept, summary now states the actual rectangle instead of claiming a screen.

name: Field_ApplySceneFade
summary: Applies the scene's fade/visibility mode to the screen state: switches the fade helper at f_78 to the wanted mode, updates the transition controller fields, resets the screen state through Field_ResetScreenState and clears the fade-in-progress bit of device+0x1346.
evidence: Field_ResetScreenState is now a confirmed name (R_021) and its own documentation names Field_ApplySceneFade as one of its two callers, which closes the loop: this is the fade application, not a generic transition.

name: maybe_Field_SetScreenFadeFlag
summary: Calls the scene virtual slot +0x0C and then sets bit 1 (0x2) of the screen-state byte at device+0x1346 - the same bit Field_ApplySceneFade clears when the fade finishes.
evidence: Field_ResetScreenState (confirmed) documents bit 4 (0x10) as the HUD-hide flag, so the old "SetUiHidden" claim is wrong; this function sets bit 1, which the named fade code owns. The exact meaning of bit 1 is still inferred, hence a vague corrected name at low confidence.

name: Gfx_SetBgLayerVisible
summary: Marks one 2D background layer as visible: validates the index against the scene's layer count, stores it at device+0xF64 and sets the matching bit in the device layer mask at +0xF68, remapping through the s8 table at +0xF84 when the remap flag +0xFE4 is set.
evidence: Gfx_ApplyBgLayerMask (0.60) implements the identical +0xF68/+0xF84/+0xFE4 bit logic and its own documentation cites this address as the single-layer variant. The new callers (sprite/model creation, overlay slot setup) pass the field 2D work and a layer index, not a menu entry, so "Menu_MarkEntrySeen" was wrong.

name: Event_ResetScreenFade
summary: Resets the event subsystem's fade state: releases the event draw nodes at +0x950/+0x964/+0x99C and sets device+0x1204 = 1 with the colour at +0x1200 cleared.
evidence: The caller is now known: Event_ResetState (0x00249AF8) calls this while resetting the event scene, which matches the "reset the fade before the next event" description. The three draw-node releases are unchanged from the first pass.

name: maybe_Ui_DrawList_MergeIntoPrimary
summary: Splices a UI draw list into the graphics context's primary UI list at device+0x100C through func_001235A4. The source register was lost by the decompiler, so only the destination is certain.
evidence: Still no caller and the argument registers are still lost (the body passes device+0x100C as both operands). The named callee Gfx_GetContext only fixes the destination; the name remains a guess.

name: Ui_DrawList_InsertNodeAt1C
summary: Inserts the draw node embedded at self+0x1C into the device's primary UI draw list (device+0x100C) with the intrusive-list insert helper 0x0010EBE4.
evidence: The readable C is truncated at halt_baddata, but the raw ARM quoted in the first pass is unambiguous (r1 = self+0x1C, r0 = ctx+0x100C, list insert) and the sibling Ui_DrawList_InsertWindowNodes at 0x00422348 does the same with +0x1C/+0x14C. Nothing in the new context contradicts it, so the name is confirmed on the assembly.

name: maybe_Ui_DrawList_MergeTwoIntoPrimary
summary: Runs the same splice into device+0x100C twice, i.e. merges two UI draw lists into the primary list. Both source operands are lost by the decompiler.
evidence: Same damaged body as 0x004215F4, no callers, source registers still lost. The name remains a structural guess.

name: Ui_DrawList_InsertWindowNodes
summary: Inserts the two draw nodes of a window (self+0x1C and self+0x14C) into the device's primary UI draw list at device+0x100C.
evidence: The two insert calls and both node offsets are visible in the readable C, and the parent/consumer 0x00421628 is now named Ui_DrawList_InsertNodeAt1C; the pointer-vs--0x18 null tests encode exactly +0x1C/+0x14C.

name: maybe_Ui_DrawList_MergeAll
summary: Second identical copy of the UI draw-list splice into device+0x100C; source argument lost by the decompiler.
evidence: Body is byte-identical to 0x004215F4, still no caller and no recovered source register; nothing distinguishes this copy from the other one, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: Ui_DrawList_InsertNodeAt8
summary: Inserts the draw node at node+8 into the device's primary UI draw list at device+0x100C.
evidence: The single insert and the +8 node offset are visible in the readable C, and the same helper/offset convention is confirmed by the now-named siblings Ui_DrawList_InsertNodeAt1C and Ui_DrawList_InsertWindowNodes.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithSpeaker
summary: Closes the message/speaker window: notifies the overlay helper 0x001DBB34, releases the cutscene message and camera through Cutscene_ReleaseMessageAndCamera/Cutscene_Teardown on self+0x70 and finishes the UI-core transition.
evidence: Three named callees now show the real work: this is a cutscene message teardown, not a face-icon/nameplate release (0x001DBB34 sits in the overlay block, not the face manager the first pass assumed). The window class is still only inferred, so the name stays maybe_ with a corrected summary.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithEmoteLine
summary: Second close variant: notifies the status window (0x001D8C80) with the message owner, releases the cutscene message/camera and tears down the cutscene, then finishes the UI-core transition. Identical to 0x0019EA58 except for the first notification call.
evidence: The body is now readable through named callees (Cutscene_ReleaseMessageAndCamera, Cutscene_Teardown, Ui_GetCore) and differs from 0x0019EA58 only in the first call, so it is a sibling close path - the "emote line" wording is not supported. Kept as maybe_ because the window class/mode is still inferred.

name: maybe_SceneTransition_SetVector3
signature: void maybe_SceneTransition_SetVector3(void* self, void* arg2, float* vec)
summary: Stores a three-float vector at self+0x84..+0x8C (default (0,2.5,0) when vec is NULL), notifies the camera/child object at self+0x40 through 0x00442CD0 and clears the state byte at +0x90.
evidence: Every caller passes the object at work+0x74 (the scene transition controller) and a float triple, and the notify callee is the named camera yaw-spring update. "Ui_Widget_SetScaleAndRefresh" described a widget that does not exist here; the corrected name only claims the structure because what the vector means is unknown.

name: maybe_SpriteActor_DispatchAction
summary: Per-frame sprite dispatch: takes the current field actor, and if its state is not 0x0D and the field UI mode is 5 it plays action sequence 0x0D with the sprite rectangle built from self->f_298; otherwise it queues gadget command 0x0C with the sprite id.
evidence: Named callees Actor_TryPlayActionSeq0D and Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand show the function chooses between two commands; it does not compute or store a screen rectangle as the old name claimed. The sprite class is still inferred from the layout, so maybe_.

name: Ui_FindObjectAtPosition
signature: bool Ui_FindObjectAtPosition(FieldWork* scene, float* position, float radius)
summary: Searches the field actor list for an object of the specific class (RTTI type 0x007C503C) whose +0x98/+0x9C coordinates lie within the query radius, returning whether such an object exists.
evidence: Callers are now named (Ui_OverlaySlot_UpdateStateMachine, Ui_Overlay_CameraFocusTask, Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState, ActorAction_UpdateMove) and all of them use this as a hit test at a position; the class filter and the |dx|<=r / |dy|<=r tests are unchanged. The list is the field actor list at work+0x54, not a UI object list, but the verb is right.

name: maybe_SpriteActor_UpdateTouchAndPosition
summary: Advances the sprite's touch state (Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState on self+0x3B8) when its state byte is 4, and when the touch query reports busy returns 1; otherwise it submits the sprite position to the current actor with Gfx_Actor_SetPosition3D.
evidence: The body is now fully readable through named callees (Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState, Gfx_Actor_SetPosition3D); it is a touch step plus position submit, not a draw check. Class still inferred, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_IsReady
summary: Runs one Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState step and returns the inverse of func_0064C740(handle), which is the "object state == 5" query. Same 28-byte body as 0x0021B510, 0x00290580 and 0x003A1CD0.
evidence: Checked all four identical bodies: they are template copies that differ only in the argument, and none has a caller. func_0064C740 is not catalogued, so its meaning ("state == 5") is only inferred; the name stays a guess.

name: maybe_Actor2D_TestStateAfterScroll
summary: Runs one Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState step on the actor and returns func_0064C740(actor) XOR 1. Exactly the same body as 0x001A3C88/0x00290580/0x003A1CD0.
evidence: No caller and the shared 28-byte body is duplicated at three other addresses; the only new information is that the callee is the temp/hit state machine, which does not settle the polarity. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_IsSpriteHidden
summary: Runs one Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState step and returns func_0064C740(spriteId) XOR 1. Same body as 0x001A3C88/0x0021B510/0x003A1CD0.
evidence: Still no caller and no readable body for func_0064C740; the name only claims a boolean query. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_IsTouchOutside
summary: Runs one Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState step and returns func_0064C740(touchState) XOR 1; the hit test itself lives in the uncatalogued callee. Same body as 0x001A3C88/0x0021B510/0x00290580.
evidence: No caller and the same body is copied at three other addresses, so this is template code, not a distinctive gadget routine. Kept as maybe_.

name: Ui_GlobalObjects_Shutdown
summary: Shuts the UI support singletons down in reverse creation order: resets the 0x28-byte task object, the 0x1EB0-byte sound sequence, the 0x80-byte icon cache and the string work, each only while its "created" flag byte is still set.
evidence: The only caller is now named Ui_Overlay_Shutdown and the callees Sound_System_Teardown/Anim_Sequence_CtorBase confirm a singleton teardown, but the name Ui_System_Shutdown is already taken by 0x00626E44 (the audio/system shutdown), so this one is named after what it actually tears down: the global UI support objects (task object, sound sequence, icon cache, string work).

name: Ui_Overlay_UpdateFlash
summary: Advances a full-screen flash overlay: samples the two-value track, writes the colour into device+0x12F0..+0x1300 and, after two frames without change, tears the overlay down and restores the default colour/size.
evidence: Caller maybe_Gfx_Overlay_EndFrame and callees Gfx_Movie_Update/Ui_Overlay_Shutdown are now named; the colour-register writes and the two-frame shutdown are unchanged, so the flash-overlay reading holds.

name: maybe_Gfx_ShutdownPainters
summary: Tears down six global render helper subsystems (0x6B87A4..0x6B989C), releases the six singleton objects and drops the object attached behind the last one through its virtual release slot.
evidence: Both callers are shutdown paths (Ui_Overlay_Shutdown and maybe_Gfx_ResetGlobalPair), which supports a global render-helper teardown, but the six 0x6Bxxxx callees are still unnamed so "painters" remains a guess. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Anim_SetStateId
summary: Switches an animation object to another state: if the previous state, its flag bit or the stored id was set it resets the controller first, then stores the new state id at self+8.
evidence: The body is unchanged and self+8 is written with arg2, but the "reset" callee is now the named Ui_Overlay_Shutdown, which is used by this class as its reset helper; the caller set (debug menu, scene field) does not reveal the class. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Action_StartCut
summary: Starts the first of two field action variants: clears the target state via 0x0023B61C, starts the animation on the owner (Gfx_Node_FaceObject with the current animation id from work+0x48+0x3B4), installs the +0x84 completion callback and, when the owner's +0x23C state is set, shows the attachment slots.
evidence: The callees are now named (Gfx_Node_FaceObject, Model_AttachSlot_ShowAll), which confirms "start an owner animation + completion callback", but the Cut/Dig label still rests on a pooled string only. Twin of 0x001BA3F4 with a different state offset. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Action_StartDig
summary: Identical flow to StartCut but keyed on the owner state at +0x238, i.e. the second field-action variant.
evidence: Confirmed as the twin of 0x001BA2D8 (same three callees, different state offset and callback label), but the actual action names are not proven, so kept as maybe_.

name: Model_SyncAllStateAttachments
summary: Makes attachment visibility match the current player state byte (work+0x48 -> +0x281): in state 0 it hides every visible slot 0..0xB plus the special slot f_274, otherwise it shows only the slot for the current state, then points f_88 at the default parameter block.
evidence: The callees are now named Model_AttachSlot_HideAll/Model_AttachSlot_ShowAll, and the per-state array at +0x244 plus the state byte from the UI manager are exactly what the name claims. The only uncertainty is the class name, which is unchanged.

name: maybe_Field_Action_EndCut
summary: Ends the first field action variant: resets the target state via 0x00239A1C and hides the attachment slots when the owner's +0x23C state is set. Mirror of 0x001BA2D8.
evidence: Body confirmed as the mirror of StartCut (same two callees, hide instead of show), but the Cut/Dig label is still unproven. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Action_EndDig
summary: Ends the second field action variant (+0x238 state), otherwise identical to EndCut.
evidence: Confirmed as the twin of 0x001BA37C; the action name is still only inferred. Kept as maybe_.

name: Ui_MonsterBook_HandleListEvent
summary: Handles the monster-book face-icon event: after the standard cancel/refresh prologue it either rebuilds the full monster list (all 0x413 monster ids, sorted), or pushes the text/decoration widget for sub-state 1, posting menu events 0x26/0x27/0x28.
evidence: The body's main work is Ui_MonsterBook_BuildEntryList/Ui_MonsterBook_SortEntryList over ids 0..0x412 plus Ui_FaceIcon_SetId, i.e. the monster book list page - not a generic face icon. The sister function at 0x00243EEC has the same prologue and is now named Ui_MonsterBook_*, which pins the family.

name: Ui_PanelGroup_Update
summary: Input/visibility update for a panel group: handles the cancel flag (+0x14 bit 2) by popping the sub-pane, toggles the selected panel on the confirm bit and re-lays out the group when the scroll grid moved.
evidence: Callees are now named (Ui_Window_PopSubPane, Ui_GetCore, Ui_ScrollGrid_MoveCursor, Ui_List_GetScrollOffset), which covers every branch of the body; the function is a per-frame widget update, matching the first-pass name.

name: Ui_MonsterBook_BuildModelList
summary: Monster-book page handler: for the selected part index it walks all 0x413 monster records, collects those whose part byte matches, sorts and submits the list, then pushes the page widget. The sister of Ui_MonsterBook_HandleListEvent with a different filter.
evidence: The named callees are Ui_MonsterBook_SortEntryList, Container_SortedInsertU16 and Ui_FaceIcon_SetId; nothing draws a model, so "DrawModel" was wrong. The 0x413-record walk with a part-byte filter is the actual work.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_CreateItemModelFromRecord
summary: Applies one layout record to a window: pops the sub-pane when the record's cancel bit is set and creates/attaches the item model with the record's three geometry fields.
evidence: The geometry call is now named maybe_Ui_ItemModel_CreateAttached, so "ApplyRecordGeometry" understated it: the function creates the item model. Kept below 0.5 because the item-model helper itself is still a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_RecordDetailWindow_HandleInputE
summary: Record-detail input handler: applies the cursor position, then selects one of three sub-lists from the row type byte and pushes the matching text widget with the style from the global descriptor.
evidence: The prologue and the three-way switch are unchanged, and the three callees are now named (maybe_Ui_TextWidget_SetTextIndex, maybe_Ui_WidgetStack_PushAt); still no caller, so the window class and the "input E" label remain inferred. Kept as maybe_.

name: BattleUnitDisplay_ValidateMember
summary: Validates the displayed unit before showing it: resolves the actor's member record, asks for the two ids from the actor vtable (+0x84/+0x88), and marks the display failed and queues event 0x1D when either lookup is missing (-1 / 0xFFFF).
evidence: Named callees now include Battle_QueueActionEx (the event it raises), Game_GetWork and the established member-record accessor func_0035EB98, and the four battle UI callers are named. The check is exactly a member/data validation.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_ReleaseList14
summary: Releases every element of the intrusive list anchored at object+0x14 by calling its virtual destructor (vtable slot +4), then stops at the sentinel.
evidence: The body is pure list teardown and the named callers (Battle_Start, Text_Scroll_UpdateStateMachine) only show it is used during battle/text teardown. The "+14" structural name is accurate but the owner class is unknown. Kept as maybe_.

name: Text_Style_MatchesId
summary: Style predicate: when the text owner has no record id it compares its stored style id directly; otherwise it maps the record's flag byte (1 -> id 2, 0 -> id 1) and tests the requested id.
evidence: Both callers are now named text windows (Text_Scroll_UpdateStateMachine, Text_TalkWindow_Update) and the data-manager lookup resolves the style record; the two mapping cases are exactly what the name claims.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SelectEntryEx
signature: void maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SelectEntryEx(UiItemScreen* item, int screen, char* flags)
summary: Main item-screen entry action: looks up the item, applies the equipment-range and ownership/party checks, performs the bag add/consume through the shop helper, then sets the follow-up command ids (0xB..0x21) on the screen state machine.
evidence: All four callers are now named item-screen handlers (SelectEntry, MoveCursor, HandleCount, ToggleCursor) and the callees Item_LookupRecord / maybe_Shop_BuyItemForMember pin the data flow, but the exact entry/command split between this and its callers is still unclear, so the "Ex" name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_LineFillChars
signature: int maybe_Text_LineFillChars(uint32_t* lineState, int fontId, uint32_t value, uint8_t mode, int count)
summary: Fills `count` characters into a text line: initialises the line state (mode/colour/value), measures the line through the glyph helpers and appends each character, with the font-0x139 special case that emits the two space codes 0xCD/0xCE and refreshes the text root.
evidence: The readable C is badly damaged here (unaff_r registers and item/member calls mixed in by the decompiler), so the naming rests on the header description and the named glyph helpers. It is still the best reading, but not trustworthy enough for 0.5. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_LineFillCharsEx
summary: Register-level twin of 0x00310844 recorded as a separate Thumb entry: same measure/append loop and the same font-0x139 0xCD/0xCE special case, but all parameters are in registers so none can be recovered.
evidence: No caller and the body is the untyped remainder of 0x00310844 (identical label, identical 0x139/0xCD/0xCE tail and the same register flow). The item/member callee names the checker notices come from this Thumb fragment's lost arguments - the same registers are the text-line buffer in the ARM twin, and the block ends by setting text cells and refreshing the text root, so this is not item code. The item reading would need an actual disassembly check before promotion.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_OpenList
summary: Opens/initialises the item list: resets the selection (id 0xFFFF, count 0, category 0xFF, cursor -1), reads the row list's current selection through Ui_ListWidget_GetSelectedItemId and chains to the screen's pager setup.
evidence: The list helpers are now named (Ui_ListWidget_GetSelectedItemId, maybe_ShopWindow_DetachPane) and match the "reset selection then show the list" reading; no caller, so the screen class remains inferred. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmBuy
summary: Confirm step of the shop list: reads the selected row id and scroll offset from the active row list (screen+0x236C or +0x23CC by category), stores them and re-enters the pager/list refresh.
evidence: The body is fully readable but every callee except Ui_ListWidget_GetSelectedItemId is unnamed, and the only caller is another shop maybe_. Name kept; class still inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_EntryMaterial_Update
summary: Updates the material/colour preview of the currently selected entry: handles the cancel/confirm flags on the entry list, applies the two text colours from the selected row values, and builds a material descriptor for the row (with the 0x5E special case) so the description pane can show it.
evidence: The body is UI widget code, not a 3D model: it drives the entry list at self+0x5AC, Ui_ApplyTextColor/Ui_ApplyTextColorAlt and Model_CreateMaterialDesc, and ends in Ui_JumonWindow_UpdateEntryDescription. "Model_UpdateAttachedParts" was wrong; the new name is deliberately vague because the owning window is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_SetupAnimTransition
signature: void maybe_Ui_Widget_SetupAnimTransition(UiWidget* widget, uint32_t animId, int mode)
summary: Pushes the widget's animation pane and sets two animation values: maps animId through func_002BBAD0 and stores it in the animation block at widget+0x13C/+0xCC0, then optionally maps and stores mode as the second value.
evidence: All ten callers are UI screens/panels (Ui_StatusPanel_ChangeMember, Battle_StatusIcon_Update, message window, spell window) that pass a widget plus two ids, and the body pushes a pane and sets animation values; "Model_SetupTransition" was the wrong subsystem. The exact animation meaning is unknown, so maybe_.

name: Ui_Sprite_Draw
signature: void Ui_Sprite_Draw(Ui_Sprite* sprite, const UiDrawRecord* rec)
summary: Draws one UI sprite from an explicit draw record: picks one of the sprite's three draw targets from the sprite mode and the record's flip/vis flags, applies the record, sets the scale and toggles the 2D layer, then restores it.
evidence: Two of the four callers are confident (Text_DrawToken, Ui_ShowInfoMessage) and use it exactly as the text/info sprite submit; the three draw targets and the virtual draw calls are unchanged.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_WantsInstantText
summary: Returns 1 for message modes 0 and non-2; only in mode 2 does it build/look up the wide-layout table and return 0 when the layout entry's +0x46 byte is 1, i.e. when the text should be revealed immediately.
evidence: The only caller is now named Text_DrawToken, which places it in the text reveal path, but the polarity (0 = instant) is still derived from the layout byte, not proven. Kept as maybe_.

name: Field_UpdateDrawList
summary: Per-frame update of the field draw list: ticks every object in the +0xD74 list, broadcasts suspend/resume to the two attached objects and the ten slot lists, collects the visible camera-facing objects, sorts them by distance and toggles their visibility mask.

name: Field_NotifyAttached24

evidence: Callers are now named (Ui_SceneFlow_Update, Ui_SceneFlow_TeardownObjects) and the function is one of the four sibling broadcasts; the slot number in the name is literally the virtual slot called.

name: Field_NotifyAttached20
summary: Same broadcast as 0x001C70F8 but for virtual slot +0x20.
evidence: Body is identical to the confirmed sibling except for the +0x20 slot; same named callers. Confirmed.

name: Field_NotifyAttached1C
summary: Same broadcast family but for virtual slot +0x1C.
evidence: Body matches the +0x24/+0x20 siblings with only the slot differing; same two named scene-flow callers. Confirmed.

name: Field_NotifyAttachedIdle8

name: Field_AdvanceSlotTimers
summary: Advances the view work one step: applies the pending rewind request (f_D80), decrements the timer f_D84, re-binds the attached objects (0x001C8584 + maybe_Field_BindAttachedObjects) and broadcasts slot +0x14.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect_UpdatePlacement
summary: Positions a screen-space effect relative to the camera: builds the effect world offset, scales the offset by the distance to the camera (clamped to a near/far range), projects it with Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen and lets the owner apply it (virtual +0x2C).
evidence: The projection callee is now named Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen and the distance source is the object at work+0x74, which supports the placement reading, but the class is still only inferred from the layout. Kept as maybe_.

name: Ui_Widget_ProjectAnchorObject
summary: Positions a world-anchored widget: resolves the actor handle at self+0xB0 in the object hash, checks the actor class, projects its +0x9C..+0xA4 position to screen space and writes the quad position (with a constant vertical offset) into the draw slot at self+0x30.
evidence: The caller is now named Ui_Widget_UpdateWorldAnchoredChildren and the projection callee Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen, which pins both halves of the name.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_UpdateBillboard
summary: Projects a UI overlay anchor into screen space: adds the animated offset at +0x6E0..+0x6E8 to the local offset, projects it and writes the quad position, then applies a per-slot parallax offset for slots 0/1.

name: Ui_Overlay_UpdateTransform
signature: void Ui_Overlay_UpdateTransform(UiOverlay* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4, float scale)
summary: Positions the active overlay slot: computes the distance scale from the slot's world anchor, tests whether it is ahead of the camera (stored as the slot visibility byte), projects it, refreshes the slot record and then applies the widget screen transform.
evidence: Named callees now cover every step (maybe_Camera_ComputeDistanceScale, Gfx_ProjectWorldToScreen, maybe_Ui_Widget_ApplyScreenTransform), and the slot index/stride match the rest of the overlay family.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ProjectWorldSlot
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_ProjectWorldSlot(UiWindow* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4, float scale)
summary: Projects the window's active world-anchored slot: computes the distance scale from the slot anchor, projects the position, refreshes the slot record and applies the widget screen transform. It is the same code as Ui_Overlay_UpdateTransform without the ahead-of-camera visibility test.
evidence: The body contains no release at all - it projects and refreshes the slot, then calls maybe_Ui_Widget_ApplyScreenTransform - so "ReleaseSlotIcon" was wrong. The corrected name only claims the structure because the owning class is unknown.

name: maybe_Model_ApplyParameterBlock
signature: void maybe_Model_ApplyParameterBlock(Model* self, int frame, int stateValue)
summary: Runs the model's parameter block: copies the record (Model_CopyParamBlock), and for the two entries compares the current frame with the entry's threshold and, on a successful battle-RNG roll, records the state value at self+0xEA4.
evidence: The named callees (Model_CopyParamBlock, Game_GetDataManager, the battle RNG roll) show a parameter block plus a random variant choice; the exact meaning of the two entries is not established. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor_UnlinkFromParentList

name: maybe_Actor_UnlinkFromParentList3

evidence: Confirmed as the mirror of 0x002793C4 with the +0x714 list offsets; same three callers and same unproven class. Kept as maybe_.

name: Actor_ResetComponents
summary: Resets the actor model's components: resets the model slots (Actor_ResetModelSlots), clears the state word at +0xE94 and, when the actor is active, runs the release virtual (+0x11C) of all 32 component pointers at +0xE9C.
evidence: The callee Actor_ResetModelSlots is now named and is also the only caller of this function, forming a clear reset pair; the 32-slot component loop is unchanged.

name: Actor_StatusBlock_Init
summary: Initialises an actor status/model block: installs vtable g_actorStatusBlockVtable, self-links the intrusive lists, clears the ids to 0xFFFF, builds the model/animation objects, resets the model slots and zeroes the ten 0x24-byte entry records.
evidence: The vtable is now symbolic (g_actorStatusBlockVtable), the two callers are named CreateStatusBlock/CreateStatusInstance, and the body ends by calling the named Actor_ResetModelSlots - the constructor reading is solid.

name: Ui_PartyStatus_RefreshIcons
summary: Refreshes the party-status icon row from the member record's status bits (poison/curse/sleep/special): calls the icon virtual +0xE4 with the matching icon ids, selects the bar mode from the member slot and copies the extra status value when bit 7 is clear.
evidence: The member record accessor (func_0035EB98, established fact) and the panel vtable 0x759AD0 family are now identifiable; this is vtable slot 2 of the panel class and every call is a status-icon update.

name: Ui_PartyStatus_AdjustValue
summary: Adjusts the gauge value shown by a party-status panel: clamps the delta to the panel range, writes the new value, refreshes the bar/colour, and when the value reaches 0 plays the empty-bar virtual and notifies the member record.
evidence: The vtable accessors +0x90 (current) and +0x94 (max) and the refresh virtuals are consistent with the first pass, and the function shares the 7-entry vtable 0x759AFC with the other panel methods. No direct caller (vtable slot), but the body is complete.

name: Ui_PartyStatus_ApplyValue
summary: Writes the panel's current gauge value back into the member record (clamped to the record maximum), and stores the selected status-icon index/value pair for the record, or resets both when the special bit is clear.
evidence: Two named callers (Actor_ReleaseAndFree, Ui_PartyStatus_Reset) and the established member accessor confirm the write-back direction; the icon index/value fields at record+0x1C2/+0x1C4 are matched by the refresh function at 0x001CE0DC.

name: Ui_Anim_UpdateFramesOnState
summary: When the requested animation range differs from the current one, plays the range-change SE and sets the animation frame of three refs (self+0x58C, self+0x5DC and self+0x50) plus the shake update, then re-syncs the attached part.
evidence: Callees are now named (Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame, Ui_AnimShake_Update, Sound_PlaySeById) and the range comparison is explicit; the name describes exactly the three frame writes.

name: Ui_MovieWindow_UpdateLayout
summary: Updates the movie window layout: ticks the three sub-animations at +0x184/+0x1D4/+0x228, adds the per-frame offset (input-dependent) to f_27C clamped to 0..3 and sets the animation frame, then switches the window state from the movie idle flag.
evidence: The named callees Os_GetGameWork/Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame and the three animation blocks are unchanged; the input bit at work+0x10 -> +0x74 and the clamp are visible, supporting the layout-update reading.

name: Ui_TwoPane_PlayBottomAnims
summary: Binds the "bottom_in" animation to the pane at self and "bottom_out" to the pane at self+0x50, then resets the animation value of both panes.
evidence: Two string literals in the body (s_bottom_in / s_bottom_out) and the named Ui_AnimRef_Bind/Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame calls prove the name exactly; no caller, but the evidence is direct.

name: Ui_Window_InitChildParts
signature: void Ui_Window_InitChildParts(UiWindow* self, const uint8_t* layout)
summary: Applies a child-part layout record to a big window: stores the layout value at +0x1964, sets the frames of the two part animations (+0x50, +0xEC) and initialises the window's row list from the layout entry when the third flag is set.
evidence: Callees are now named Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame and Ui_RowList_InitRows, which covers both halves of the body; the layout record fields used are unchanged.

name: Ui_SideCrossFade_Begin
signature: void Ui_SideCrossFade_Begin(UiSideCrossFade* self, uint8_t* leftVisible, uint8_t* rightVisible, int slot)
summary: Starts a two-sided cross-fade: enables the left or right pane, picks animation slot 0..2 from the argument, sets that pane's visible flags and starts the corresponding tween while the other pane is reset.

name: Ui_Widget_ResetPair
summary: When the ownership check 0x00630B04(self, self+0x980) succeeds, resets the two child widgets at +0x930 and +0x8E0 (stop the shake tween, set the frame, snap the value).

name: maybe_Ui_List_UpdateSubWidgets
summary: Formats the list's row container at +0x124, resets its second state, updates the animation ref at +0x174 and then calls the owner virtual +0x24.
evidence: The body does not release anything: it formats the row model, sets the animation frame and then calls the owner virtual, so "ReleaseSubWidget" was misleading. Corrected to a vague update name because the caller (Ui_SpritePart_CreateFromDesc) does not explain the class.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimNode_Release
summary: Destroys the animation node embedded at self+0x4C (0x00649BD4) and then resets its animation ref.
evidence: The same two-call pair is used on the same node type at 0x0028A244, but neither callee is named beyond the anim-ref setter, so the release reading is still inferred. Kept as maybe_.

name: Ui_TimerDisplay_SetTimeFromCentiseconds
signature: void Ui_TimerDisplay_SetTimeFromCentiseconds(TimerDisplay* self, float value, float scale)
summary: Splits value*scale into minutes/seconds/centiseconds (division by 6000 and the 10/100/1000 fixed-point constants) and pushes the six digits into the six digit panes at self+0x50 with stride 0x9C.
evidence: The fixed-point constants (0x57619F1/6000, 0x10624DD3/1000, 0x51EB851F/100, 0x66666667/10) and the six Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame calls are unchanged, and the name matches them exactly.

name: Ui_Tween_SetSpeeds
signature: void Ui_Tween_SetSpeeds(Tween* self, float speed, float b, float c)
summary: Clamps three incoming values to 0..1, stores the resulting tween speeds at +0x4C/+0x50 and +0x58/+0x5C (base 0.3 multiplied by the clamped values), resets the tween object and applies them.
evidence: The clamp branches and the fixed 0.3 factor are unchanged, and the only caller (maybe_Ui_DungeonHpWindow_AnimateRows) uses it to set row animation speeds; the name describes the work.

name: Ui_Element_ApplyCommand
signature: void Ui_Element_ApplyCommand(UiElement* self, const UiCommand* cmd)
summary: Applies an element command: bit 1 of the command flag byte shows the element decoration at +0x64, bit 2 clears it, and the element at +8 is faded in; a float payload above 0.9999 marks "already at target".
evidence: The handler is registered in the table at 0x0072B364 and both branches now resolve to named animation calls (Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame, Ui_AnimShake_Update), matching an element command handler.

name: Fs_AsyncIo_Register
summary: Reserves an async-IO slot: queries the free-slot state, marks the per-object slot byte, installs the embedded list head at +0xC and initialises the 0x1000/0x10 transfer context. Returns whether the slot was obtained.

name: Fs_FileRequest_Init
summary: Initialises a file-request object: stores the flags at +0x4C, installs the embedded list head at +0xC/+0x44.. and starts the 0x1000-byte / 0x10-aligned transfer context through the shared 0x10EAB0 initialiser.
evidence: The caller is now named Fs_FileRequest_Update and the body is the same initialiser pair as the confirmed Fs_AsyncIo_Register (same 0x1000/0x10/0xFFFFFFFE arguments), so "Os_SyncObject_Init" (an SDK sync object) was wrong: this is the file-request context.

name: Ui_OverlayManager_Reset
summary: Resets the UI overlay manager at work+0x48: clears the row id/flag fields, copies the saved UI mode bytes into f_281/f_282, and (re)allocates its three work buffers (800/100/100 words) plus the 25-entry parameter table.
evidence: The caller Ui_MessageWindow_CloseAll passes work->f_48, and the object has the UI overlay manager's mode byte at +0x281 (established fact). The three buffers and the global pair template are unchanged, so "Party_Status_Open" was the wrong subsystem.

name: maybe_ViewWork_Reset
summary: Resets the view/camera work at work+0x4C: clears its flag byte, resets the two screen-view collections at +0x54/+0xB10, restores the invalid id defaults and frees every node of the +0x1640 list.
evidence: The caller (Ui_MessageWindow_CloseAll) passes work->f_4C, and this object is the one the camera functions use (f_15CC view entries, f_163C list), so "MenuView" was wrong. The class has no proven name, hence a vague corrected name and maybe_.

name: Ui_Core_GetOrCreateChild
summary: Lazily creates and caches the 0xF4-byte child object at uiCore+0x10: allocates it from the core's heap, constructs it with class descriptor 0x00782234 and returns the existing instance on later calls.

name: maybe_Ui_Pane_Hide
summary: Minimal hide step: clears the visible flag at +0x14, sets the animation state to 2 (0x001A1774(f_C,2,0)) and marks the pane stopped at +0x10.
evidence: The only caller is Ui_MessageWindow_CloseAll, which passes work->f_58; the function is a three-write hide, but what object work+0x58 is is not established. Kept as maybe_.

name: Camera_ApplyWorkEntries
summary: Builds and applies the camera work entries for the view work: for each of the 0x20 candidate slots it tests visibility, resolves the indexed handle, fills the camera setup record and calls Camera_SetupFromRecord, registering the resulting path.
evidence: Every branch now resolves to named camera functions (Camera_IsCandidateVisible, Camera_UpdateWorkPath, Camera_SetupFromRecord) and the 0x1C-stride entry math is unchanged, so "Ui_ApplyRowLayout" was the wrong subsystem: this is camera work.

name: Camera_UpdateWorkEntry
signature: uint32_t Camera_UpdateWorkEntry(ViewWork* self, CameraOutput* out, int entry, int target)
summary: Fills one camera output record from a work entry: computes the entry address from the view id and entry index, resolves the indexed handle, copies the path/offset/orientation fields and calls Camera_UpdateWorkPath.
evidence: Three named callers (Camera_UpdateTargetList and the two follow-position functions) and the named Camera_UpdateWorkPath callee confirm the entry update, and the entry formula matches 0x001D15AC.

name: Camera_FindEntryCoveringPosition
signature: int Camera_FindEntryCoveringPosition(ViewWork* self, float* position, int mode, int targetId, int flags)
summary: Returns 1 when the position lies inside one of the camera work entries: it filters the 0x24 entries by the mode bit (and the target-height byte when a target id is given) and compares the squared distance against the entry's radius (+0x4EC or +0x4F4).
evidence: The body is a containment test over the camera entries, not a follow-distance calculation: it returns a boolean and never writes a distance. The named callers (Camera_UpdateWorkPath and the follow-position functions) use it to select the covering camera entry.

name: maybe_Field_ApplyToActorsInRadius
signature: void maybe_Field_ApplyToActorsInRadius(FieldWork* scene, float* position, int filter)
summary: Walks the field actor list and for every actor of the target class within the squared radius calls func_005E7848(actor,2,0) and the actor's own virtual +0x98. Used by the slide-window transitions to affect the actors around a point.
evidence: The callees show an actor-list radius walk with a fixed operation applied to each hit, not a view lookup, so "Gfx_FindViewByDistance" was wrong. The operation itself (0x005E7848) is still unnamed, so the corrected name is deliberately vague.

name: maybe_Field_DetachActorsInRadius
signature: void maybe_Field_DetachActorsInRadius(ViewWork* self, float* position, int filter)
summary: Walks the field actors around a position and detaches the ones of the matching class: decrements the per-entry counters (f_15E0/f_15E4), clamps the entry height counter, and clears the attachment through Field_AttachSlotObject.
evidence: The body decrements view-entry counters and calls the named Field_AttachSlotObject, i.e. it removes actors from the view entries - not a look-at computation. Called by the talk-camera release path. The class name remains inferred, so maybe_.

name: Camera_RebuildWorkList
summary: Rebuilds the camera work list: drains the pending list at +0x163C, then for every nearby actor of the target class allocates a 0x50-byte work node, copies its transform from func_00178880 and appends it.
evidence: The body first clears and then repopulates the +0x163C list, so "ClearWorkList" described only the first half; the per-actor copy and the named Mem_AllocAligned_2/Os_GetGameWork calls are visible and the only caller is the talk-camera release.

name: maybe_ViewWork_AddRowsFromBuffer
signature: void maybe_ViewWork_AddRowsFromBuffer(ViewList* list, ListHead* head, uint32_t alloc)
summary: Copies up to 0x20 row descriptors from the embedded 0x1C-stride buffer at list+0x100 into freshly allocated 0x18-byte list nodes and appends them, skipping the 0x0FFFFFFF "empty" rows.
evidence: The caller is now named Field_TalkCamera_ReleaseWork and passes the two screen-view lists of the view work, which fixes the data source but not the class; the body itself is a generic row copy. Kept as maybe_.

name: Camera_SetTargetFromHandle
summary: Sets the camera target for a battle transition: resolves the actor handle, increments the view-entry usage counter and clears its attachment via func_005E7848, then copies the field scene node position into +0x1618..+0x1620 and the data-manager value into +0x15D8.
evidence: Both callers are named (Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle, maybe_Battle_CreateEnemyDisplay) and the body ends by writing the three target position words - a target setter, not a handle resolver. The named Field_SceneNode_GetPosition supplies the position.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_UpdateBattleTrigger
summary: Polls the object's battle trigger: if the per-map flag byte (work+0x2A4E6+index) is 1 or 4 it returns the channel busy state; otherwise it starts the trigger once via 0x0059AA14 and on later frames calls Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle(&self->f_29C).
evidence: The completion call is the now-named Field_BattleTrigger_StartBattle and the started flag is f_29A, so this is the trigger object's per-frame poll rather than a generic field-flag wait. The per-map table read is still only inferred, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_ConstructRowTable
summary: Constructs a 4x6 array of 0x5F9720-type elements on the stack, using the game work as the source when the alternate flag is 0. The decompiled body ends in the array constructor, so the consumer is not visible.
evidence: The body contains no text/string formatting at all: it is one std_ConstructArray(dst, 0x5F9720, 4, 6) call, so "FormatTableString" was unsupported. Corrected to a structural name at low confidence because the 4x6 element type is unknown.

name: maybe_Math_Vector3_Interpolate
signature: void maybe_Math_Vector3_Interpolate(float* a, float* b, float t, uint32_t arg3)
summary: Builds a 12-byte vector on the stack from one input (func_0039CD08) and then combines it with the second input and the interpolation factor through func_0039CBBC.
evidence: The five callers are all camera-orientation/model-part code passing vectors, so this is a vector helper; the callee names printed in the readable C (Text_LayoutSingleLine) are clearly wrong for that context. Still uncertain which of the two inputs is scaled, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_Layout_SetLineLimit
signature: void maybe_Text_Layout_SetLineLimit(uint8_t* lineCounter, TextLayout* layout, uint32_t limit)
summary: Stores the line budget in the layout state and returns early when the current line index already reached it or exceeds three; otherwise it constructs the next line record on the stack (the decompiler marks the constructor as noreturn).
evidence: The named caller Text_LayoutSingleLine and the line counter/limit logic are unchanged, but the tail is a damaged std_ConstructArray call whose destination is lost, so the function does more than its name claims. Kept as maybe_.

name: Model_UpdateBlinkTimer
summary: Ticks the character's blink and expression timers: decrements the blink countdown, toggles the open/closed state, re-arms from the randomised range, advances the expression state and calls Model_UpdateFaceAnimation when anything changed.
evidence: Four named callers (Gfx_RenderObject_Update, Model_Attach_UpdateChildren, maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateModel, maybe_Model_AttachSlot_ReleaseNode) all run per-frame character updates, and the named Model_ApplyFaceParamQuad/Model_UpdateFaceAnimation close the face pipeline.

name: Model_Attach_UpdateChildrenRoot
summary: Root guard for the child update: when the slot is the chain root (f_654 == 0) it forwards to Model_Attach_UpdateChildren and always returns 1.
evidence: The callee is now named Model_Attach_UpdateChildren and the thin wrapper convention (return 1 as a vtable update) is visible in the 24-byte body.

name: Model_SetFaceId
summary: Applies a face id to the model: sets it on the global face manager (work+0x4C) and stores the low byte in the model's face block at self+0x70.
evidence: The caller Field_Npc_UpdateFace and the two-call body show a setter for a face id, not a "record" read; the second call is the face-block setter. Name corrected accordingly.

name: Sound_ResolveFieldBgmId
signature: void Sound_ResolveFieldBgmId(BgmState* state, const BgmRecord* record)
summary: Resolves the background-music track for a map/scene record: picks the day/night or field variant from the record's bytes, honours the player's music setting and stores the chosen track id in the state.
evidence: Two named field-scene callers (Ui_MessageWindow_ShowTalkData, Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene2) and the named Sound_GetPlayer setting check support the BGM resolution reading, and the record/track fields are unchanged.

name: maybe_Field_CreateTalkRecord
summary: Lazily creates the shared 0x98-byte talk/UI object (vtable 0x00782A08) when the record's first byte is 1, clears its map flag, then initialises the talk state at self+0x14, starts the pending view and applies the object at self+0xB8.
evidence: The only caller is the named Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene2 and the shape is a lazy singleton plus three setup calls, but two of the three callees are unnamed and the last two names printed by the decompiler look wrong. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_PrepareSpriteContext
summary: Prepares the scene flow's 0x80-byte sprite context once (lazy allocation through func_00384050) and advances the step through func_00383A58, returning 0 while the step runs and 1 when the ready flag at +8 is clear.
evidence: The caller Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene2 and the lazy-allocation guard are unchanged, but both real callees are unnamed, so what the step object does is inferred. Kept as maybe_.

name: Field_ResetTalkState
summary: Resets the field talk/event state before the next scene: refreshes the UI overlay slots (work+0x48), selects the character on the field scene (work+0x88), registers the actor tables and forwards the map-jump event record at self+0x18.
evidence: The named callees (Field_HandleMapJumpEvent, Ui_StatusWindow_SelectCharacter, maybe_Model_RegisterActorTables) and the sole caller Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene2 now cover the whole body, confirming a talk-state reset at scene open.

name: Ui_BattleTargetWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor: installs the class vtable, destroys the embedded 4x2 sub-widgets through Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub, unlinks the five intrusive lists and tears down the nested page/state objects before the base destructor.
evidence: Callees are now named Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub, Ui_Object_DtorBase and std_destroy_range, and the vtable/unlink/delete sequence is the standard destructor shape; only the battle-target class identity comes from the thunk name.

name: Ui_TalkWindow_DtorB
summary: Talk-window destructor: installs the class vtable, releases the two sub-widgets, destroys the embedded pane range (2 entries) and two list pairs, then runs the base destructor and frees the object.
evidence: The named callees (Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub, Ui_Object_DtorBase, std_destroy_range) plus the operator-delete tail make the destructor reading certain, but the plain name Ui_TalkWindow_Dtor is already used at 0x002187D0, so this second talk-window destructor gets the B suffix used elsewhere in the project for template copies.

name: Ui_PartyHpGaugeWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the party HP gauge window: releases four inner widgets, destroys the four 0x260-byte member slots, installs the base vtable, unlinks three list pairs, then runs the base destructor and frees the object.
evidence: Named callees Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub/std_destroy_range and the four-slot layout (matching the sibling at 0x001D7490) confirm the destructor; the class name comes from the HP-gauge family.

name: Menu_ItemSelect_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the item-select window: installs the class vtable, releases the ten slot widgets and the five detail-row widgets, destroys both ranges, unlinks the list pairs and runs the base destructor.
evidence: The body is a destructor (vtable store, Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub loops, std_destroy_range, Ui_Object base dtor) and its only caller is the destructor thunk maybe_Menu_ItemSelect_Construct. "InitAnimations" was the opposite of what the code does.

name: Ui_ListWindow_DtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of a list window: installs vtable 0x0076216C, destroys the base object at +0x138, unlinks the three list pairs, destroys the 0x50-byte container/sub-object and frees the window.
evidence: The vtable store, the Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub call and the Ui_Object_DtorBase/operator-delete tail are all visible and the callees are named; the destructor reading is solid. Ui_ListWindow_Dtor already exists at 0x0029F240, hence the B suffix for this second list-window destructor.

name: Ui3D_ApplyModelVisibility
summary: Re-applies the node's pending model-visibility flag to the scene model (visible = f_6FE), clears the flag, and fires the "cbhm_arm_alive" and "cbhm_mask_alive" model animations so the character's arms/mask follow the state.
evidence: The named callees Container_KeyedList_SelectEntry and Model_Attach_PlayAnimation plus the two string literals make the body explicit; this function is the derived twin of the base implementation at 0x005F7E88.

name: Field_Actor_ResetHomePosition
summary: Puts a field actor back on its home placement: writes the default speed/turn constants, copies the stored home position (+0x220..+0x228) over the current position, raises the dirty flag, re-applies the orientation block and marks the transform dirty.
evidence: The body is exactly the home-position copy plus the two named calls (Field_SceneNode_NotifyChildrenUpdate, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection), which supports the name without new assumptions.

name: Gfx_Node_ApplyModelVisibility
summary: Base implementation of the node visibility update: applies the pending f_6FE flag to the scene model (visible/hidden), clears the flag, calls the common node update and clears the owner's animation lock at f_160+0x536.
evidence: The body is the base version of the now-named Ui3D_ApplyModelVisibility (0x004E43B8), which its own header documents as the derived twin with the same body; "StopAnimationAndDetachOwner" described effects the code does not have.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetVirtual
summary: Virtual reset override: broadcasts the child update (0x005E7598) and then tail-calls the widget's own virtual slot +0x84 with the constant 0x007BE72E.
evidence: The tail call target and the constant are still not recoverable (Ghidra reports an unrecovered jump table), so whether this is a reset or a mode set is unknown. Kept as maybe_.

name: Gfx_TrailMesh_BindBaseCallbacks
summary: Initialises the trail-mesh base node: runs the common node update, binds the "cbhm_base" pane through virtual +0x70 and installs the per-frame callback through virtual +0x84.
evidence: The "cbhm_base" string literal, the two virtual slot calls and the Gfx_TrailMesh family context (0x0028CF34) support the name; no caller because it is a vtable initialiser.

name: Field_Actor_UpdateEffectState
summary: Shows or hides the actor's attached effect from its state byte: states 3 and 4 play the model animation, set the effect visible and enable/reset/loop the effect object; every other state hides the effect.
evidence: The state test and the three named effect calls (func_003BF390/003BF3C0/003BF35C are unnamed but the virtual +0x74 "set visible" is consistent) are unchanged, and the callerless vtable context matches the N_049 reading.

name: Field_Actor_RestartActionSequence
summary: Stops the actor's running child sequences (base node broadcast) and immediately starts the default sequence with func_005E74A0(actor,0,1).
evidence: The 32-byte body is a two-call restart and the second callee is now the same sequence starter used by the action code; the name describes it.

name: maybe_Model_Actor_PlayEquipAnimation
summary: When the actor reports ready (virtual +0x34 non-zero) it installs one of two state callbacks through virtual +0x84, chosen by the byte at self+0x88.
evidence: The body selects between two callback addresses from one flag byte; it does not play an animation directly, so "PlayEquipAnimation" is only a guess. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_UpdateTransform
summary: Scene-node update: runs the base node update and, when the element list at self+0x89 is non-empty, forwards it through the node virtual +0x84.
evidence: The body is a base update plus one conditional virtual tail call, and the class/vtable (0x7683D4) is not confirmed as the guide window. Kept as maybe_.

name: Field_Actor_UpdateVisibility
summary: Vtable slot 10 of the field actor class: runs the base node update and sets the embedded object's visibility state to 2 when the actor flag at +0x220 is 1, otherwise to 0.
evidence: The flag test and the virtual +0x18(state) call are fully visible, and the function is one of the four vtable entries shared by the field actor class tables; the visibility reading holds.

name: maybe_Ui_GoldTextWindow_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the gold-text window: runs the scene-node base update, re-attaches the node transform and dispatches the window virtual +0x40 with argument 4.
evidence: The body is a scene-node update plus a virtual dispatch, not a destructor, so "Dtor" was wrong. The neighbouring Ui_GoldTextWindow_InitPanes supports the class, but the virtual argument 4 is unexplained, hence maybe_.

name: Ui_TextListWidget_AttachPane
summary: Binds the widget to its layout pane: runs the common node update and calls virtual +0x70 with the pane name descriptor 0x007BFCEE.
evidence: The body is the standard "bind named pane" pattern (same as Gfx_TrailMesh_BindBaseCallbacks) and the string descriptor is the only argument; the class is inferred from the layout family.

name: maybe_Ui_RowObject_CtorB
summary: Constructor of a small row object: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x007662B0, constructs the animation-ref list at +0x4C and marks the row visible.
evidence: The caller Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor (confident) confirms a row object of the sakusen window, but "CtorB" is a placeholder and the class has no better name yet. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TabBar_Ctor
summary: Builds a small UI object with three animation-ref lists: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs the class vtable and chains three Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor calls, returning the object base.
evidence: The body constructs lists and returns the base - it finds nothing, so "FindTabBar" was wrong. The three-list object matches the tab-bar layout the old name referred to, but that class is not proven, hence maybe_.

name: Ui_GuideWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the guide window: allocates the 0x138-byte object, installs the class vtable, initialises three circular list heads and constructs the embedded message object.
evidence: The caller is now named maybe_Ui_EnsureSubObject and the allocator/ctor pair is visible; the class name still comes from the guide-window family, but the constructor shape is clear.

name: Ui_Panel_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small panel object: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x00768510 and constructs the two animation-ref lists at +0x4C and +0x9C.
evidence: The caller maybe_Ui_PanelMessageWindowCtor and the two-list layout confirm a small panel object; the matching destroy code at 0x003AA3E0/0x003AA40C releases exactly these two sub-objects.

name: Ui_Window_CtorWithThreeParts
summary: Constructor of a UI window that owns three consecutive 0x50-byte animation-ref sub-objects (+0x54/+0xA4/+0xF4): installs vtable 0x0076DE64, clears the two fields at +0x4C/+0x50 and constructs the three parts.
evidence: The three chained Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor calls and the +0x50 stride are exactly what the name describes; no caller, but the shape is unambiguous.

name: Ui_Window_CtorWithSubobject
summary: Constructor of a UI window with one embedded sub-object: installs vtable 0x00771B4C, constructs the animation-ref block at +0x4C and initialises its transform fields (0,0,1).
evidence: The single Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor and the field initialisation are visible; the name describes the layout and the vtable confirms the class family.

name: Ui_StatCompare_Create
summary: Allocates the stat-compare widget (vtable 0x00773178) and constructs its two animation-ref panels at +0x47 and +0x97, returning the object base.
evidence: The caller is now named Ui_EquipTextWindow_Ctor, which owns the equipment comparison screen, and the two-panel layout matches; the allocator/ctor structure is unchanged.

name: Ui_TwoAnimListWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a UI window with two animation-ref lists at +0x4C and +0x9C: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase and installs vtable 0x0077DAD8.
evidence: The object base, vtable and two chained Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor calls make the two-list constructor reading exact; the UI-window constructor table reference supports the class.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimObject_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small animation object: stores the vtable, constructs the embedded animation-ref list at +5, points the three frame pointers at the default frame and clears the state fields.
evidence: The body is a plain constructor whose only callee is Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor; the class is unknown and the caller list is empty, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Menu_InitLayoutNode
summary: Initialises a small layout/child node: stores the id, constructs its animation-ref child at +5, sets the child flag and clears the four preceding words.
evidence: The body is a constructor/init with one named callee and no caller (vtable slot 1 of a 10-entry table), so the "menu layout node" class remains a guess. Kept as maybe_.

name: Ui_RankIcon_Ctor
signature: UiRankIcon* Ui_RankIcon_Ctor(uint8_t* self, int unused, int rank, int id)
summary: Constructor of a rank icon: stores the rank, the 0xFF "empty" byte, the id and the rank again, then constructs the embedded pane object at +0xC.
evidence: The four field writes and the single Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor call are visible and the paired binder 0x00290F40 supports the icon reading.

name: maybe_Battle_Popup3D_UpdateRootEx
summary: Alternate entry of the 3D battle popup update: on the constructor path it initialises the gauge-bar fields, otherwise it finds the first free popup slot, applies the slide offset and finishes it through virtual +0x2C.
evidence: The body mixes a constructor half and an update half (Ghidra merged two entries at a Thumb boundary) and uses unaff_ registers, so the split is not reliable. Kept as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoListObject_Ctor
summary: Constructs a small UI object with two animation-ref lists: chains two Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor calls and returns the object base.
evidence: The body only constructs two lists - it finds nothing, so "FindDialogObject" was wrong. Nothing identifies the class, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_EmotionBalloon_Init
signature: int maybe_Ui_EmotionBalloon_Init(EmotionBalloon* self, uint32_t unused, uint32_t owner)
summary: Initialises the emotion-balloon object: stores the owner pointer, clears the state word and constructs the embedded animation-ref list at +8.
evidence: The body is an initialiser/constructor (owner store, clear, Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor), not a reset of an existing object. The class name comes from the paired balloon code, so the corrected name is still a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_LocationWindow_CreateChild
summary: Creates a child object of the location banner: installs the secondary vtable 0x007682DC, constructs the animation-ref element at +0x11C with the given style and returns the banner base.
evidence: The caller Ui_SubObject_Create and the vtable pair (0x7682DC right before the banner vtable 0x7682E0) support the reading, but the child's role is still unproven. Kept as maybe_.

name: Ui_AnimRefList_Init
summary: Initialises an animation-ref list: stores the owner, constructs the embedded list through Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor, self-links the three sentinel nodes and loads the default timing pair.
evidence: The single named callee Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor and the sentinel/timing initialisation are exactly what the name says; no caller because it is an embedded initialiser.

name: Ui_Window_Create4Sub
summary: Allocates a window (vtable 0x00775640), stores the flag byte at +0x47, constructs the chain of four animation-ref sub-widgets and the trailing number block, and returns the object base.
evidence: The caller is now named Ui_PokerWindow_InitCardPanel and the four Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor calls plus the number block are visible; the name describes the layout.

name: Ui_Widget_ApplyScreenTransform
signature: void Ui_Widget_ApplyScreenTransform(UiWidget* widget, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, GfxMatrix* out)
summary: Builds a screen-space transform from the widget rectangle at +0x98 (inverse width/height as scale plus the centre translation), applies it to *out and then to the layout element, so child content maps onto the rectangle.
evidence: Five callers, two of them confident (Ui_Widget_UpdateAnchorAndTransform, Ui_Widget_UpdateWorldAnchoredChildren), and the named Ui_LayoutElement_ApplyTransform callee confirm the transform application.

name: Ui_StatusWindow_ApplySlotFrames
summary: When the slot flags are dirty, applies one frame per slot: visible slots get the "shown" object set and the camera entry rebuild, hidden slots get the remove call and the row layout, for all 17 slots, then clears the dirty flag.
evidence: The named caller Ui_StatusWindow_SelectCharacter and the named slot helpers (Ui_StatusWindow_AddSlotObjects/RemoveSlotObjects, Camera_ApplyWorkEntries) cover both branches, confirming the per-slot frame application.
